name: org.machanism.machai:ghostwriter
description: Machai Ghostwriter is a Java 8 AI-powered, project-aware command-line application and embeddable processing library for repository-wide automation. It scans source code, tests, Markdown documentation, HTML/XML, PlantUML, Python, TypeScript, text guidance files, configuration, and other selected project artifacts. In Guidance mode, it discovers durable inline @guidance instructions using format-aware reviewers and submits the associated file context to a configured GenAI provider. In Act mode, it runs reusable TOML-defined workflows with ordered episodes, inheritance, prompt substitution, controlled tool access, project-scoped context, and optional interactive execution. Ghostwriter supplies project-bound file operations, safe command execution, web and REST retrieval, targeted patching, workflow control, and report/log support. It is suited to repeatable documentation generation, code and test maintenance, repository review, and CI/CD automation. The published application is a Maven JAR with org.machanism.machai.gw.processor.Ghostwriter as its command-line entry point; the pack profile creates gw.jar.

constructors.description: Creates a guidance processor that scans a project for supported files containing @guidance comments and delegates requests to the selected GenAI provider.

examples.description: Create a processor from an embedding application after supplying an initialized configurator and provider/model identifier.

constructors.description: Creates an Act processor for reusable TOML workflows, including episode execution, inherited Act properties, and project-aware tool access.

examples.snippet: org.machanism.machai.gw.processor.ActProcessor processor = new org.machanism.machai.gw.processor.ActProcessor(new java.io.File("."), "OpenAI:gpt-5.1", configurator); processor.setAct("task Review documentation");

features.name: Ghostwriter command-line entry point
features.signature: static void org.machanism.machai.gw.processor.Ghostwriter.main(java.lang.String[] args) throws java.io.IOException, org.apache.commons.cli.ParseException
features.description: Runs Ghostwriter as a command-line application. Guidance mode is the default; --act selects a named TOML workflow. CLI settings for project directory, model, instructions, exclusions, threads, Acts location, and scan paths override persisted configuration.

examples.snippet: java -jar gw.jar "glob:**/*.md" --projectDir . --model "OpenAI:gpt-5.1" --instructions "Keep headings consistent and preserve links."
examples.description: Run a non-interactive Guidance-mode scan for Markdown files in the current project.

examples.snippet: java -jar gw.jar --projectDir . --model "OpenAI:gpt-5.1" --act "task Review the project documentation"
examples.description: Run an Act-mode task against the current project.

features.name: Scan documents
features.signature: void org.machanism.machai.gw.processor.AIFileProcessor.scanDocuments(java.io.File projectDir, java.lang.String path) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Scans a project directory using a relative path, absolute in-project path, glob pattern, or regex pattern and processes matching artifacts with the configured processor.

examples.description: Limit an embedded processor to project site Markdown documents.

features.name: Configure and execute an Act
features.description: Loads and configures an Act by name. Acts can come from bundled resources, local or remote Act locations, or a TOML path; syntax supports prompt text, selected episodes, and task shorthand.

examples.snippet: processor.setAct("review#1,3! Check concurrency and error handling");
examples.description: Select episodes 1 and 3 of a review Act and stop after the selected episodes.

features.name: Apply targeted patch
features.signature: java.lang.String org.machanism.machai.gw.tools.FileFunctionTools.applyPatchToFile(java.io.File file, java.lang.String patch, java.lang.String charsetName, java.io.File projectDir)
features.description: Applies a unified diff or simplified exact search-and-replace patch to an existing project file, enabling narrow, reviewable AI-driven updates.

examples.snippet: new org.machanism.machai.gw.tools.FileFunctionTools().applyPatchToFile(new java.io.File("README.md"), "@@\n-Old text\n+New text", "UTF-8", new java.io.File("."));
examples.description: Replace an exact line in a project README using a simplified patch.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.gw.reviewer.Reviewer
studs.description: Service-provider contract for format-specific extraction of @guidance instructions from a project file. Implementations report supported extensions and return normalized prompt fragments.

customizations.name: Reviewer service provider
customizations.description: Implement org.machanism.machai.gw.reviewer.Reviewer and register it through Java ServiceLoader to add guidance extraction for another file format.

examples.snippet: public final class com.example.CustomReviewer implements org.machanism.machai.gw.reviewer.Reviewer { public java.lang.String[] getSupportedFileExtensions() { return new java.lang.String[] { "custom" }; } public java.lang.String perform(java.io.File projectDir, java.io.File file) throws java.io.IOException { return null; } }
examples.description: Define a reviewer for the custom extension, then add its fully qualified class name to the Reviewer service-provider configuration.

examples.title: Install, configure, and run the Ghostwriter CLI
steps: Download and unpack the Ghostwriter CLI pack from https://sourceforge.net/projects/machanism/files/machai/ghostwriter/gw.zip/download, or build the project with Maven using mvn -Ppack install to produce target/gw.jar.
Install a Java 8 or newer runtime and make java available on PATH. Configure credentials and endpoint settings required by the selected Machai GenAI provider.
From the target project, run java -jar gw.jar --help to inspect the available command-line options.
Add an HTML comment containing @guidance: to a supported file such as a Markdown page, then run java -jar gw.jar "glob:src/site/**/*.md" --projectDir . --model "OpenAI:gpt-5.1".
Review the resulting file changes and rerun with a narrower path, exclusions, or revised guidance as necessary.
examples.description: This scenario uses default Guidance mode to process documentation instructions stored beside the files they govern.

examples.title: Run a reusable Act in CI
steps: Create or select a TOML Act that defines instructions, inputs, and a non-interactive project path.
Store provider credentials in the CI system's secret store and expose only the environment variables required by the provider configuration.
Invoke java -jar gw.jar --projectDir . --model "OpenAI:gpt-5.1" --act "your-act-name" in a CI job.
Run validation such as mvn test after Ghostwriter, inspect the generated diff, and publish or commit accepted changes through the pipeline's normal review policy.
examples.description: Acts provide an ordered, versionable workflow suitable for unattended repository automation.
